# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 73 (Bi-Vb Pc73)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc73
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 73
**Title (English, from literature):** Ordaining a trained unmarried woman without approval
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 73 (*Paripuṇṇavīsativassa-sikkhita-kumāribhūta-asammata*) defines an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) incurred when a nun ordains an unmarried girl without obtaining the formal authorization of the Order. Specifically, the rule stipulates that even if an unmarried maiden (*kumāribhūtā*) is fully twenty years of age and has completed the requisite two-year probationary training in the six rules, she must still be granted the formal agreement or permission to ordain (*vuṭṭhānasammuti*) by the Saṅgha of nuns before receiving full ordination [Hüsken 1997]. Ute Hüsken notes that this rule has no counterpart among the monk's rules and does not introduce new restrictions beyond those established in rules such as Pācittiyas 63, 64, and 71; rather, it clarifies that the age qualification of twenty years does not exempt a candidate from the requirement of formal Saṅgha authorization [Hüsken 1997].

In addition to an English translation by Bhikkhu Brahmali, the rule is paralleled within the Pali canon in Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha Pācittiya 73 and Bhikkhunī Parivāra Pācittiya 73. Vinayas of other early Buddhist schools contain direct parallels, including the Dharmaguptaka (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 130), Mahīśāsaka (Pācittiya 103), Sarvāstivāda (Pācittiya 112), and Mūlasarvāstivāda in both Chinese (Pācittiya 110) and Tibetan (Pācittiya 75) recensions.
